newsitem.title: USA: New York Dist court says Texaco arraignment Tues.
newsitem.headline: New York Dist court says Texaco arraignment Tues.

text.p: The U.S. District Court for the southern district of New York in White Plains said Tuesday that an arraignment at around noon Tuesday was expected in the Texaco Inc race bias case, though a court spokesperson couldn't immediately say whether there had been any arrests in the case.

"If someone has been arrested I don't know about it; but we wouldn't know until a half-hour before the arraignment," said an official in magistrate judge Lisa Smith's office. "The pre-arraignment matters haven't been concluded yet."

Texaco spokesman Chris Gidez said that the company was not aware if any criminal charges had been filed. He said Texaco had been subpeonaed for information and had supplied that last Tuesday, Gidez said.
Assistant attorney Stanley Okula is handling the case, an official at the U.S. Attorney's Office said.
Last Friday, Texaco settled a civil case brought against it originally in 1994 by around 1,400 employees from ethnic minorities for an estimated total cost of $176 million.

The case came to national attention several weeks ago when the plaintiffs released a tape in which a number of current and former Texaco officials allegedly discuss destroying documents related to how minorities at the company were treated. The tape sparked a federal criminal probe.
